evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/auth.rs:699 — the login handler returns 401 ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED for a suspended account BEFORE verifying the password (password check starts at line 713). Any caller submitting an arbitrary password for a suspended email gets a distinct ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED response, whereas an unknown email gets the generic INVALID_CREDENTIALS — an account-enumeration oracle for suspended users.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/auth.rs:750-756 — this is the exact anti-pattern the code deliberately guards against elsewhere: the email-verification gate was moved to AFTER the password check (with a comment citing #956) precisely because returning a status-specific error pre-password turns login into an enumeration oracle. The suspended-account branch was not given the same treatment, so it still leaks account existence pre-authentication.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes — ~437 handler error arms return the raw error via ErrorResponse::new("DB_ERROR"|"INTERNAL_ERROR"|"DATABASE_ERROR", e.to_string()) in the client-facing JSON body (≥21 route files: budgets.rs:260-704 (~15 arms), emergency/broadcasts.rs:158, ai/workflows.rs:46, etc.). e.to_string() on a sqlx/db error exposes internal detail (SQL fragments, column/constraint names, connection info) to unauthenticated or low-privilege API clients — an information-disclosure smell that also makes error responses non-uniform. Compare auth.rs which correctly returns a static "Login failed" and logs %e server-side only.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/emergency/broadcasts.rs:158 — Json(ErrorResponse::new("DB_ERROR", e.to_string())) returned to caller after deactivate_broadcast fails; representative of the systemic pattern.

deferred_findings.note: backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/auth.rs:700-736 — every session_repo.record_login_attempt(...) on the failure paths is fire-and-forget (`let _ = ...await`). If that write fails, failed logins go unrecorded, silently weakening brute-force/lockout accounting with no telemetry. Below the per-run cap this slice.
